docs.title: How Terra works
docs.lead: The members' app for a community treasury: chip in, ask for money, approve it. What each part does, and where the limits are.
docs.card.quickStart: Sign in, open a group, chip in, request money and approve.
docs.card.tiers: Fast lane up to {small}, the council up to {mid}, a full vote above.
docs.card.payouts: Live NEAR Intents quotes for recipients on other chains.
docs.card.real: Every claim here links to a transaction on NearBlocks.
docs.what.p1: Terra is a members' app for a community treasury. It sits on top of a group's existing Sputnik DAO: it never holds the money and never deploys its own multisig. Money only moves through the DAO's own proposals and votes.
docs.what.li1: Members see one balance in dollars, chip in, request money and approve requests.
docs.what.li2: Each member's record, computed from the DAO's own history, decides how much approval a request needs.
docs.what.li3: A live NEAR Intents quote shows what a recipient on another chain would get.
docs.what.li4: A public board shows every payout, with a receipt on chain. No sign-in needed.
docs.what.p2: Any Sputnik DAO works: type its account on the landing page. Groups without a DAO can start one in three steps with Start a group.
docs.quickStart.step1: Sign in with a NEAR wallet. Intear works on phones, Meteor on desktop. You can look around a demo group without signing in.
docs.quickStart.step2: Open a group or start one. Connect an existing DAO by its account, or use Start a group: name it, list the council and trusted members, review and sign one call. It needs at least 6 NEAR, and about 5.4 NEAR stays locked to store the contract.
docs.quickStart.step3: Chip in. Home → Chip in sends NEAR straight to the DAO account. The balance and Activity update.
docs.quickStart.step4: Request money. Pay → who, how much in dollars, and what for. It's filed as a DAO proposal, and Terra tells you which approval lane it takes.
docs.quickStart.step5: Approve. Approve lists open requests with their tier, who asked, their record and the approvals so far. When enough members approve, the DAO pays out on its own.
docs.quickStart.share: Any group opens from a link with its DAO account in it. Share it with members:
docs.code.label: Link to any group
docs.tiers.p1: Terra routes each request by its size in dollars and by the requester's record.
docs.tiers.fast.name: Fast lane
docs.tiers.fast.text: One nod from a trusted member other than the requester. The requester needs a clean record.
docs.tiers.council.name: Council nod
docs.tiers.council.text: The council approves at its usual threshold.
docs.tiers.full.name: Full vote
docs.tiers.full.text: The council votes at its normal threshold. The request stays on the public board while it's open.
docs.tiers.p2: A small request from someone with no record yet goes to the council instead. Terra also blocks approvals the treasury can't cover, since the vote would fail.
docs.tiers.note.title: The tier limits are checked by Terra, not by the contract.
docs.tiers.note.body: Sputnik decides approvals by role and proposal kind, not by amount. On chain, one trusted vote can approve a transfer of any size, so keep the trusted list small. Terra keeps council members out of the trusted role, because otherwise one council vote would also count as a trusted nod. For a hard limit enforced on chain, use <link>allowances</link>.
docs.record.p1: Every member's record is computed only from the DAO's own history: its full list of proposals, plus chip-ins found in its transactions on NearBlocks. Nothing is stored by Terra, and every row links to its proposal or transaction.
docs.record.li1: Requests filed, paid and turned down.
docs.record.li2: NEAR chipped in, and the total paid out to you.
docs.record.li4: Standing: Council, Trusted or New, from your roles in the DAO.
docs.record.p2: A clean record means you're on the council or the trusted role, or you've had at least one request paid and none turned down. A clean record is what opens the fast lane. Records key on your NEAR account; a profile name is shown too, but the account id always stays visible.
docs.joining.step1: A member opens Members → Invite, which shows a QR code and a join link.
docs.joining.step2: You open it and see the group, its balance and members, then tap Sign in to ask. That files a request to add you to the group.
docs.joining.step3: The council approves it in Approve. Your "Waiting for approval" card updates by itself and turns into "You're in".
docs.joining.p1: Groups made with Start a group take join requests from the start. For other DAOs, a council member first taps Let people ask to join in the Invite sheet; one council vote turns it on. You don't need to join to chip in or file a request.
docs.payouts.p1: When you request money, the recipient can pick a token on another chain, such as USDC on Solana. Pay asks NEAR Intents for a live quote: what they get exactly, how much NEAR the treasury sends, the fee and the time. The quote refreshes on a timer and is saved with the request, so approvers see the same numbers.
docs.payouts.p2: On mainnet, the treasury pays the Intents deposit address and the recipient gets the token on their own chain. This demo runs on NEAR testnet, which NEAR Intents doesn't support, so here the payout is the quoted amount in NEAR, sent to a NEAR account named on the Pay screen.
docs.payouts.p3: If the quote service is down, Pay shows a clearly labelled sample quote instead of a live one.
docs.allowances.p1: The group can give a member, or an AI helper, a small budget. Payments inside it skip the vote. Allowances live in a small contract the DAO owns, and setting one up or changing it is a normal DAO request.
docs.allowances.li1: Enforced on chain: a daily cap, a most-per-payment and an end date.
docs.allowances.li2: Freeze: any council member can freeze an allowance instantly. Only the DAO can change limits or unfreeze.
docs.allowances.li3: AI helper key: a NEAR access key that can only call the allowance's pay method, with a small gas allowance. It can't send NEAR, call anything else or go over its budget.
docs.allowances.p2: Dollar amounts aren't on chain: caps are stored in NEAR, converted at the price when the request is filed. A "day" is a UTC calendar day, and budgets share one pool.
docs.earn.p1: Money the group isn't using can be staked with a validator. Earn files a DAO request to stake it, and members approve it like any other request. The stake and rewards show in Earn.
docs.earn.p2: Rewards arrive once per epoch (about 12 hours), so a fresh stake shows close to zero at first. Unstaking isn't in the app yet.
docs.social.p1: All three live on NEAR Social and are signed by your own wallet. Terra has no backend.
docs.social.li1: Profiles: a name, avatar, short bio and links, saved to your standard NEAR Social profile, so they show in other NEAR apps too.
docs.social.li2: Comments: a thread on each request, also shown on the Board. Plain text, up to 280 characters. Comments from people outside the group are folded away.
docs.social.li3: Private messages: one-to-one between members, end-to-end encrypted in your browser. Your secret key is made in your browser and never leaves it.
docs.social.note.title: Privacy limits of private messages
docs.social.note.li1: Contents are encrypted, but who messages whom, and when, is public.
docs.social.note.li2: The ciphertext stays on chain for good, and there's no forward secrecy.
docs.social.note.li3: A new device or browser needs setup again; messages sent to the old key only open on the old device.
docs.social.note.li4: Clearing site data loses the key.
docs.social.note.li5: Each message is one wallet-signed write, up to 500 characters of plain text.
docs.real.p1: Each of these ran end to end and is a transaction you can open on NearBlocks.
docs.real.readme: The full list, with how each piece fits, is in the <link>README</link>.

members.how.title: How standing works
members.how.body: A first request goes to the council. After one paid request and nothing turned down, someone's requests up to {small} take the fast lane: one nod from a member of the trusted role who isn't them. Requests up to {mid}, and bigger ones, need the council's majority; big ones stay on the public board while open. The council and the trusted role are set in the DAO's policy, and every record is computed from the DAO's own history on NEAR.
members.how.limits: The dollar limits are checked by Terra. On chain, one trusted vote can approve a transfer of any size, so keep the trusted list small. For a hard cap enforced on chain, give a member an allowance instead.
members.how.noTrustedCouncil: This DAO wasn't set up by Terra and has no trusted role, so there is no fast lane: its council decides every request at the DAO's own thresholds.
members.how.noTrustedRoles: This DAO wasn't set up by Terra and has no trusted role, so there is no fast lane: the roles that can vote decide every request at the DAO's own thresholds.
members.roleHelp.member: Listed as a member. Their record starts here; small requests take the fast lane once one is paid.
members.roleHelp.trusted: Can give the one approval a small request needs. Their single approval pays any transfer on chain, so only pick people the group trusts with that.
members.roleHelp.council: Decides mid and large requests by majority, and can change the group.

landing.hero.badge: For clubs, teams and communities<wide> · built on NEAR</wide>
landing.hero.line1: A shared money pot for your group,
landing.hero.lead: Chip in together, ask for money when you need it, and approve payouts as a group. No one person holds the cash.
landing.how.title: From treasury to payout{br}in four steps.
landing.how.lead: No new wallet for the group and no contract of our own. Terra sits on top of the Sputnik DAO you have, or creates a standard one for you.
landing.how.connect.title: Connect or start a treasury
landing.how.connect.text: Type your DAO's name, or start one in a minute. Members sign in with their NEAR account.
landing.how.chipIn.title: Members chip in
landing.how.chipIn.text: Everyone sees one balance in dollars, and where every cent went.
landing.how.request.title: Ask for money
landing.how.request.text: Say what it's for and who gets paid. A live quote shows what they receive.
landing.how.approve.title: Approve and pay
landing.how.approve.text: Enough approvals and the treasury pays out itself. No one holds the keys alone.
landing.chain.title: They get paid in what{br}they actually use.
landing.chain.lead: A designer wants USDC on Solana. A venue wants NEAR. Terra shows a live quote before anyone approves, so the group knows exactly what leaves and what arrives.
landing.chain.point1: Amounts in dollars first, tokens second
landing.chain.point2: USDC on Solana, Base, Ethereum, or NEAR
landing.chain.point3: The quote is saved with the request
landing.approvals.title: Trust is earned,{br}so approvals scale with it.
landing.approvals.lead: Each member has a record, built from the treasury's own history: requests paid and requests turned down. A clean record opens the fast lane for small amounts.
landing.tier.smallText: Once you have a record, one trusted member approves and the treasury pays right then.
landing.tier.midText: A council majority signs off. First requests start here too.
landing.tier.largeText: A council majority votes, and it stays on the public board while it's open.
landing.approvals.note: Terra checks these limits. On chain, one trusted vote can approve a transfer of any size, so keep the trusted list small; allowances add a hard cap the contract enforces.
landing.faq.title: Questions, answered.
landing.faq.lead: The short answers. Everything else is in the docs.

landing.story.title: One group, one pot, four steps.
landing.story.lead: A real example: a city club paying a designer for a meetup poster.
landing.story.s1.title: Everyone chips in
landing.story.s1.text: Priya's club puts money into one shared pot. Everyone sees the balance.
landing.story.s2.title: Someone asks for money
landing.story.s2.text: Ravi asks for $20 to pay a designer for the meetup poster.
landing.story.s3.title: Members approve
landing.story.s3.text: Two members tap Approve. Small, everyday requests need fewer votes.
landing.story.s4.title: The money goes out
landing.story.s4.text: The designer gets paid straight from the pot, even in USDC on Solana.
landing.why.title: Why not just a bank account or one treasurer?
landing.why.b1.title: Nobody holds it alone
landing.why.b1.text: The money sits in your group's own account. Paying it out takes members' approval, not one person's login.
landing.why.b2.title: Everyone sees every payment
landing.why.b2.text: Every chip-in and every payout is visible to all members, with a public receipt.
landing.why.b3.title: Pay anyone, anywhere
landing.why.b3.text: Pay people in the coin they want, on the chain they use, with a live price before anyone approves.
faq.what.a: An app for groups that share money, like a club or a meetup crew. Members chip in, ask for money and approve each other's requests, and every payout is public.
faq.holds.a: Your group does. The money sits in your group's own account on NEAR, and Terra never holds it. If Terra went away, the money and its history would still be there.
faq.approve.a: Small requests from members with a good record need one trusted member's OK. Bigger ones go to the council. Every request and vote stays on a public record.
faq.chains.q: Can I pay someone on another chain?
faq.chains.a: Yes. NEAR Intents shows a live quote of exactly what they'll get, like 20 USDC on Solana, before anyone approves. On testnet the payout itself goes out in NEAR.
faq.start.a: No. You need a free NEAR account and a wallet such as Meteor or Intear, and amounts are shown in dollars. You can look around without an account.
faq.cost.a: Terra takes nothing. You only pay NEAR's network fees, a fraction of a cent each. Starting a new group locks about 5 NEAR to store its account on NEAR.
faq.open-source.a: Yes, under the MIT license. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/somewherelostt/terra).
faq.real-money.q: Is this live with real money?
faq.real-money.a: Not yet. Terra runs on NEAR testnet, so the money is test money; the cross-chain quotes are real. Mainnet is next.
landing.oss.title: Open source
landing.oss.text: Terra is open source under MIT. Read the code, fork it, run your own.
